candidate.scope: The middle miCLIP-m6A row of the assigned RNA Modifications schematic: sheared methylated cellular RNA, anti-m6A binding and UV crosslinking, immunoprecipitation, and truncation-bearing cDNA. The neighboring MeRIP-Seq/m6A-seq/m6A-RIP and Ψ-seq/PSI-seq rows are contextual, not target alternatives. iCLIP is a library-preparation component described by the matching sources, not another target workflow. The drawing ends at cDNA; downstream library completion and sequencing are not separate depicted operations.

operations.label: Add anti-m6A antibody
operations.description: Add anti-m6A antibodies to RNA fragments, forming antibody-bound RNA complexes at recognized methylated sites.
operations.mechanism: Antibody recognition precedes UV crosslinking; addition alone is not the covalent marking step.
operations.information_effect: Biological target recognition is physically associated with the RNA fragment.

operations.label: UV 365 nm
operations.description: UV exposure converts the bound antibody–RNA association into a covalent crosslink. The source caption says UV 365 nm; the matched primary implementation explicitly uses 254 nm, retained as correction c_uv rather than silently changing the caption.
operations.mechanism: UV-induced antibody–RNA crosslinking in purified cellular RNA, rather than an endogenous protein interaction in intact cells; the primary-supported implementation uses 254 nm.
operations.information_effect: A protein mark is fixed on RNA near the antibody-recognized modification, providing the lesion later read by reverse transcription.

operations.label: Immunoprecipitate
operations.description: Recover the antibody-crosslinked RNA complexes as an enriched population for subsequent cDNA preparation.
operations.information_effect: Selects antibody-associated RNA fragments; enrichment alone does not identify an exact modified nucleotide or establish perfect specificity.

evidence.locator: Results, Validation of m6A residues identified by miCLIP, [b00032]
evidence.quote: CIMS and CITS miCLIP identified six and five of the eight SCARLET-positive sites, respectively. Importantly, none of the 15 SCARLET-negative sites were called by CIMS miCLIP and only one by CITS miCLIP.

operations.label: Reverse transcription truncated at binding sites
operations.description: Convert the enriched RNA fragments into cDNA, with reverse transcription stopping at crosslink-associated sites. This broad depicted interface compresses intervening antibody digestion: the primary source attributes the RT obstacle to residual peptide on RNA, not an intact antibody being copied.
operations.mechanism: Proteinase K treatment releases RNA while crosslinked peptide fragments remain. Reverse transcription of this RNA can terminate at the retained peptide mark; the final blue fragments are DNA products.
operations.information_effect: cDNA sequence identifies the source RNA region; its crosslink-induced truncation boundary carries the positional mark. With an antibody-characterized endpoint relationship, mapped cDNA boundaries support single-nucleotide site localization (the paper characterizes SySy truncation at +1 relative to m6A). The drawing does not specify the antibody clone or an exact coordinate offset, so that calibration is primary-paper context rather than a literal label. Antibody-dependent marking can also report m6Am; truncation alone does not chemically distinguish all internal m6A from cap-proximal m6Am or guarantee that every site is recovered.
